families.topic: identifying, monitoring and protecting patients who are more vulnerable before and during cold weather
families.page_title: Supporting vulnerable people before and during cold weather: for healthcare professionals
evidence_points: Healthcare managers should establish methods to identify, alert and monitor people most vulnerable to cold-related illness.
Appropriate data-sharing agreements can support coordinated protection of vulnerable people.
Cold-weather risk should be recorded in care plans where relevant.
Plans may include monitoring room temperature and clinical observations in suitable settings.
Patient-facing staff should identify vulnerable people on their caseloads and arrange support.
Home visits can include checks of room temperature, medicines, food supplies and access to warm accommodation.

families.source: UKHSA cold-weather guidance for adult social care managers
families.topic: business continuity, risk identification and protection of adult social care clients during cold weather
families.page_title: Supporting vulnerable people before and during cold weather: for adult social care managers
evidence_points: Cold weather can worsen existing disease and increase injury risk from falls.
Managers should maintain and, when needed, activate cold-weather business-continuity plans.
Cold exposure can increase risks of heart attacks, strokes, chest infections and breathing problems.
Older people and people with cardiovascular, respiratory, mental-health or disability-related vulnerabilities may be at higher risk.
Services should identify vulnerable clients and arrange appropriate protection and support.
Risk identification should be reviewed regularly and may include a register of people requiring additional support.

families.page_title: Supporting vulnerable people before and during cold weather: for those providing services to rough sleepers
evidence_points: People sleeping rough may have chronic conditions that are worsened by cold and increase susceptibility to infection.
Local Severe Weather Emergency Protocol activation can trigger additional accommodation.
Severe-weather accommodation can be used to connect people with primary care and screening services.
Night shelters should apply infection-prevention principles and provide appropriate ventilation.
Services may extend opening hours to provide additional daytime protection.
Staff should be trained to recognise hypothermia, frostbite and other cold-related health problems.

families.topic: emergency planning, infection prevention and protection of vulnerable children during adverse cold weather
families.page_title: Supporting vulnerable people before and during cold weather: for teachers and educational professionals
evidence_points: Cold can increase risks of respiratory infections, skin conditions and mental-health problems in children.
Children aged 5 years and under are particularly vulnerable.
Damp and underlying medical conditions can increase cold-related health risks.
Education settings should maintain emergency plans for cold, snow and ice.
Settings should promote vaccination, hand hygiene and respiratory hygiene.
Staff should be trained to identify vulnerable children and use effective Cold-Health Alert dissemination systems.
